title: Horror as British Airways flight has 'near miss' with 'UFO' at 5,800 feet
excerpt: The mysterious silver object was the "size of four toasters," a report said.
content:
Emily Wright

Updated Sun, October 25, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC

A transatlantic flight carrying hundreds of holidaymakers came within feet of catastrophe after a mystery airborne object shot past the aircraft shortly after taking off from Heathrow Airport, a safety report has revealed. The British Airways Boeing 777-300ER was climbing out of the UK's busiest airport en route to New York when the flight crew spotted the bizarre metallic object screaming towards them at high speed. The packed passenger jet, carrying 256 passengers and crew, was ascending through 5,800 feet over Guildford, Surrey, when the near-disaster unfolded in broad daylight. The stunned captain urgently contacted air traffic controllers after the mystery projectile hurtled past in the opposite direction, coming within feet of tearing into the airliner's right wing.

According to the pilot's report, the object passed no more than 50 feet above the aircraft's altitude, travelling at blistering speed. Official logs show the pilot immediately radioed the London Terminal Control Centre (LTCC) to report that a high-speed projectile had buzzed the right-hand side of the wide-body jet.

The object was described by cockpit crew as "shiny silver", highly reflective, and approximately "the size of four toasters". While the crew initially feared the airborne hazard might have been an errant drone, aviation investigators admitted they were left baffled by the object's appearance and extraordinary altitude.

Following a probe into the June 24 incident, the UK Airprox Board (UKAB)-the official watchdog tasked with investigating near-misses in British skies-classified the event as a serious safety scare. Investigators officially ruled that they were unable to verify what the bizarre object actually was, warning that a devastating crash had been avoided purely by chance.

In their formal assessment, the Airprox Board concluded: "In the Board's opinion, the reported altitude and/or description of the object were such that they were unable to determine the nature of the unknown object. The Board considered that providence had played a major part in the incident and/or a definite risk of collision had existed."

Miraculously, the flight crew maintained control of the Boeing 777 and safely completed the eight-hour transatlantic crossing, touching down at New York's JFK International Airport without injury. However, the chilling incident is just one of several alarming encounters that have struck UK skies in recent months, according to the Sun.

Just days prior to the transatlantic near-miss, another passenger flight was plunged into chaos when an Airbus A320 descending into Heathrow came within yards of an unidentified dark object. The encounter was so sudden and severe that the pilot instinctively ducked in fear of an impending impact.

Months earlier, a high-ranking RAF pilot was also left stunned when a mystery craft shot past his aircraft during a delicate, high-altitude refuelling mission.
